prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name one single “best” broker for everyone, because the right broker depends on your needs (individual vs. employer, Medicare, specific doctors, budget) and where in the Kansas City area you are (KC spans both Kansas and Missouri). I can, however, help you find a great broker and tell you how to choose one. Quick options and next steps:

1) Quick question
- What kind of coverage do you need? (Individual/family marketplace, employer/small-group, Medicare, Medicaid, short-term)
- What ZIP code are you in (or which side of KC — KS or MO)?
If you tell me those two things I can suggest a few local brokers/agencies to contact.

2) Where to look now
- For Marketplace plans: HealthCare.gov has local agents/navigators who are certified to enroll people at no cost.
- For Medicare: Contact your state’s SHIP (State Health Insurance Assistance Program) for free, unbiased counseling.
- State insurance department sites (Kansas Insurance Department and Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance) let you verify licenses and complaints.
- Google/Yelp/Better Business Bureau for local reviews, and ask friends/family for referrals.

3) What to prefer in a broker
- Independent broker (represents many insurers) vs captive agent (represents one company). Independent usually gives more plan choices.
- Licensed in KS or MO (whichever you need) — verify with the state site.
- Experience with your situation (e.g., chronic conditions, specific hospitals, Medicare).
- Will provide written plan comparisons (premiums, deductibles, out-of-pocket maximums, networks, drug formularies).
- Offers ongoing support for claims and renewals.

4) Questions to ask a broker (short list)
- Are you independent or do you represent specific carriers?
- Which carriers/plans do you typically recommend in my ZIP code and why?
- How do you get paid? (Most are paid by the carrier; confirm no extra fee.)
- Can you show example quotes and network/coverage differences for my doctors and prescriptions?
- Do you help after I enroll (claims, appeals, annual renewals)?

5) Red flags
- Pressure to pick one plan immediately.
- Vague answers about licensing or fees.
- Refusal to show multiple plan options or network details.

If you share your ZIP code and the type of coverage you need, I’ll pull together 3–5 brokers/agencies in Kansas City to contact and draft a short script you can use when calling them.
